newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close slightly lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close slightly lower in thin trade.

text.p: Thai stocks dipped marginally in thin trade on Friday as investors sold large capitalised communication and finance issues ahead of a long weekend, brokers said.

The composite SET index eased shortly after the market reopened in the afternoon and it closed 1.19 points lower at 660.10 on lacklustre 2.4 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index dropped 0.20 point to 48.72.
"Investors decided to get out in the afternoon, reluctant to to hold stocks during this long weekend holiday," said Thaneit Khantigaroon of Ekachart Finance.
The market will close on Monday on the Coronation Day holiday.

Brokers said persistent market concern over weak first quarter earnings of non-financial stocks due for release later this month also induced selling. Banks and finance firms announced their first quarter results in late April.
Brokers said the index, hitting an intra-day high of 666.08 or up 4.79 points shortly after the morning opening, moved in a narrow range during the rest of the day.
Declines led gainers 173 to 114 with 85 ending steady.
The banking sector rose 0.11 percent, the communication sector slipped 0.41 percent, and the finance sector retreated 1.31 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list closing unchanged at 172 baht, Jasmine International fell 0.75 to 35.75, PTTEP dropped two to 312, and Dhana Siam lost 0.75 to 28.75.
